clue.text: 45 degrees, round about "brown" temperature

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
C is short for circa, Latin for about
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A geometry note about an angle, with a stray remark about brown temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighth of a full circle is a sector spanning forty-five degrees, the instrument and arc named for that fraction.

clue.text: American city bird highly excited when feet are scrubbed

indicators.note: in a down clue each word's foot is its last letter, and scrubbing wipes those final letters away

parts.note: a chick is a young bird
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: A bird gets wildly excited once its feet have been scrubbed clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when feet are scrubbed' removes the last letter of each word: CHICK loses K and AGOG loses its final G, leaving CHIC and AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windy City on Lake Michigan is a major metropolis in Illinois, USA.

clue.text: A range of odds and ends, essentially jumbled

indicators.note: jumbled says the letters picked out are mixed into a new order
the essence of the phrase is its central core, here the middle five of its eleven letters

explanation.surface: A scrappy collection of odds and ends, thrown together in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the central five letters of ODDSANDENDS, SANDE, and 'jumbled' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American mountain chain is a range of peaks along the continent's western side.

clue.text: Get a buzz from this "relief" drug, acid from the chemist?

parts.note: relief is a let-up; in a down clue LET written up reads TEL, which the quotation marks flag
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a chemist would call a strongly acidic solution pH one

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a high from a pain-relief drug, perhaps acid bought at the pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around "relief" mean read it as 'let up': in a down clue LET placed upward gives TEL. On a chemist's pH scale a reading of 1 is strongly acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone rings or buzzes with incoming calls, so it is the device that gives you a buzz.

clue.text: Settle back on bed, held by mum from Gretna?

indicators.note: held by says the bed-and-settle pieces sit inside the word for mum

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means hush, written SH

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: back says the word for settle is read from right to left

parts.note: to settle in a seat is to sit

explanation.surface: Someone settles back on a bed, cradled by their mother from a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle back' looks like relaxing; it is a reversal. Gretna Green is a Scottish border village famous for runaway weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretna lies just over the border in Scotland, so someone from there is a Scot by nationality.

clue.text: Constant peril suggested by present-day extremists?

explanation.surface: A warning that today's radicals pose an ever-present threat.
explanation.walkthrough: The unchecked letters down the far left and right of the grid spell OVERHANG and HANGOVER: 'present-day extremists' points to those extreme columns of today's puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Damocles sat under a sword hung by one hair, a byword for looming danger; the grid's outer columns, its extremists, spell OVERHANG and HANGOVER, things that hang over.

clue.text: Heads of operations hunted men in charge of resistance?

indicators.note: heads of the three words are their opening letters, stacked at the top in a down clue

explanation.surface: Leaders of a manhunt are put in charge of the Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance' looks like the wartime Resistance; it is electrical resistance, measured in units named after Georg Ohm.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to electrical resistance as measured in ohms, the unit named after physicist Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Collection made by an artist, not before time

indicators.note: the artist does not come before time, so the time letter leads the painter's name

parts.note: Henri Rousseau was a French painter

explanation.surface: An art collection assembled by a painter who arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not before time' reads as an idiom for overdue; here it says the artist is not placed before T, so T comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's gathered store of clothes and linen for married life is a collection put together before the wedding.

clue.text: After short trip, little weight put on by a philosopher

indicators.note: after places the weight below the trip in this down clue
in a down clue the weight is set on top of the letter A

parts.note: a spin is a brief drive or outing
oz, an ounce, is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: After a quick outing, someone gains a little weight thanks to a philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a 17th-century Dutch rationalist thinker, author of the Ethics.

clue.text: Curry — see whence it might come the second I missed the toilet

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references

indicators.note: the second letter I of the country is dropped while the first stays

parts.note: curry is associated with India as its home
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone eats a hot curry and then, in a hurry, misses the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second I missed' removes the final I of INDIA, leaving INDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery dish of Goan origin, a very hot curry on British menus.

clue.text: Complaint in Olympia left out for review

indicators.note: to review is to look over again, here to rework the remaining letters
out says that letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A grievance raised at the Olympia exhibition hall is dropped for later review.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of OLYMPIA to leave OYMPIA, then 'for review' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sightedness is an eye condition, and a condition can be called a complaint.

clue.text: Each ram munching oats ultimately does this

definitions.text: Each ram munching oats ultimately does this

indicators.note: munching puts the oats letter inside the ram's mouth

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word oats

explanation.surface: Each ram munching on oats in the end polishes them all off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a ram munching oats finishes the food.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food entirely is what a hungry ram does to its oats.

clue.text: Judgement made by heartless 19

explanation.surface: A ruling delivered by a heartless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is the answer to 19-down, CHOCICE; remove its heart, the middle C, to get CHOICE, another word for this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A judgement is a ruling reached, and a choice is something resolved upon, both meanings of a verdict-like conclusion.

clue.text: Polish declaration that drinks are cancelled?

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up, then announces there will be no more drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish a piece of work is to finish it neatly; a round of drinks being off means no more are bought.

clue.text: Countryman worn out by new age travelling around island

indicators.note: out says the letters of worn are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around says the reshuffled letters enclose the island letter
travelling sends these letters moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rural man worn out by New Age travellers circling an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman' suggests a rustic, but here means a national. 'out' and 'travelling' are two separate anagram signals, with 'around' putting I inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Here a countryman means a compatriot, someone from a particular country, Norway.

clue.text: Base one's madness mainly on legend?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: read as leg end, the end of a leg is a toe

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: rage is a fit of madness or fury

explanation.surface: Someone bases their madness mostly on a myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' must be split into 'leg end'; TOERAG is British slang for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a contemptible scoundrel, a low or base person.

clue.text: Paraphernalia that's robust, top to bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the top letter is moved to the bottom

parts.note: strapping means big and robust

explanation.surface: Sturdy gear that has been turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter S of STRAPPING moves 'top to bottom', to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the accessories and outward trimmings that go with something, its paraphernalia.

clue.text: Animal stopped by a husky

indicators.note: stopped by says the animal is plugged by the letter A inside it

parts.note: a horse is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal is halted by a husky dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' looks like the sled dog; it means rough-voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky.

clue.text: In which you might drill instruction for a mechanic?

explanation.surface: Something to drill into, or orders shouted to a garage mechanic.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore drilled to extract petroleum; split as two words, it tells a mechanic to lubricate thoroughly.

clue.text: Port or rum up cloaca

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink of port or rum goes up a sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like a drink beside 'Port', but it is the adjective meaning strange, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific resort city on Mexico's coast with a harbour, so a port.

clue.text: Selection box for cold cold sweet

indicators.note: box says the selection encloses the cold letter

parts.note: a choice is a selection
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A selection box of sweets meant to be kept cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Selection box' looks like a box of chocolates; 'box' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small block of ice cream coated in chocolate is a frozen treat.

clue.text: Tweak, say, old close friend

parts.note: to tweak something is to alter it slightly
say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: Someone adjusts what an old close friend said.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for other self, used for an intimate friend almost a second self.

clue.text: Ecstasy added to brown bread to cause euphoria

indicators.note: in a down clue the ecstasy letter is added on top of the next piece

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
brown bread is Cockney rhyming slang for dead, and late means dead

explanation.surface: A drug is slipped into brown bread to give a high.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown bread is Cockney rhyming slang for dead; LATE also means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with great joy, producing a euphoric mood.

clue.text: A ballerina missing a Nobel Prize winner

indicators.note: missing says a letter has gone from the dancer's name

parts.note: Anna Pavlova was a famous Russian ballerina

explanation.surface: A ballerina is absent from a Nobel ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: PAVLOVA loses its final A to leave the name of Ivan Pavlov, the physiologist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology for work on digestion.

clue.text: Regularly viewed rash changes in opinion

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, starting from the first of viewed

explanation.surface: A rash that keeps being looked at shifts people's views.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to swing round; these are shifts of direction, as in views.

clue.text: Slimy, wet creatures damaged retina

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters of retina are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: Slimy wet creatures have damaged someone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of sea snails living in wet coastal places, slimy molluscs.

clue.text: Heath plant round country in which tits might nest?

parts.note: ling is heather, a heathland plant

indicators.note: round says the country is turned about and read backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A heather patch near a country where birds might build their nests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tits' looks like the birds, with 'nest' and 'Heath plant' feeding that picture; it is slang for breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear includes bras, which cradle the breasts.

clue.text: Looks around pound for animal disease

indicators.note: around says the looks wrap the pound letter

parts.note: a gander is slang for a look
L stands for libra, the pound sign

explanation.surface: Someone peers around an animal pound looking for disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious bacterial infection of horses and mules.

clue.text: One responsible for tender organisation?

parts.note: tender suggests money or bids, but it is about tending patients: a senior nurse running a ward

explanation.surface: Someone who handles a company's bids.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior nurse in charge of a hospital ward, who organises the care given.
